links.outcome: Pass rate on expert-curated variant interpretation questions with vs without curated database tool grounding
links.effect: gpt-oss-20b achieved a 94% pass rate with MARRVEL-MCP versus 41% without; lightweight models (3B-20B) with tools matched or outperformed larger models without tool access.
links.quote: A 20B-parameter model (gpt-oss-20b) achieved a 94% pass rate, versus 41% without MARRVEL-MCP, approaching state-of-the-art proprietary performance.

unlisted_practices: Tool-augmented context engineering (MCP tool interface to curated genomic databases) so small LLMs match larger models

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the effect of adding structured domain tools and context engineering (MARRVEL-MCP) to LLMs versus running LLMs without tool access on 100 expert-curated genomic questions.

primary.practice: tool-augmented context engineering / external tool grounding
